title: refactor(comments): split comments_bloc.dart into three focused blocs
body:
## Description

Carves the 1,462-line `CommentsBloc` into three focused successor blocs composed via `MultiBlocProvider`, with cross-bloc coordination going through `BlocListener`-bridged outbox signals per `.claude/rules/state_management.md`'s no-BLoC-to-BLoC dependency rule.

### Successor blocs (each under 500 lines)

| Bloc | Lines | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `CommentsListBloc` | **497** | Canonical `commentsById` store, load / paginate / sort / real-time stream / EOSE tracking, plus six new store-mutation events received from the two other blocs' outbox signals (`OptimisticCommentInserted`/`Confirmed`/`RolledBack`, `CommentReplacedInStore`, `CommentRemovedFromStore`, `CommentsRemovedByAuthorFromStore`). |
| `CommentComposerBloc` | **498** | Main / reply / edit input state, two-tier mention search (`restartable()`), publish + edit publish flows; emits `ComposerOutbox{Insert,Confirm,Rollback}Placeholder` / `ReplaceComment` for the UI to bridge into list-bloc store mutations. |
| `CommentReactionsBloc` | **388** | Vote / vote-counts fetch / report / block / delete with `droppable()` transformers; emits `ReactionsOutbox{RemoveComment,RemoveByAuthor}` for list cleanup after block + delete. |

### Outbox bridging

`_OutboxBridges` in `comments_screen.dart` wires two `BlocListener`s that translate composer / reactions outbox state changes into `CommentsListBloc` events, then dispatches `ComposerOutboxConsumed` / `ReactionsOutboxConsumed` to clear the signal. The bridge also re-dispatches `CommentVoteCountsFetchRequested` onto `CommentReactionsBloc` whenever the loaded comment set changes (replaces the previous self-add inside `CommentsBloc._onLoadRequested`).

### Helper extractions (pure-Dart, no bloc dependency)

To keep each bloc under the issue's 500-line acceptance criterion:

- `comments_list/throttled_subscription.dart` — token-bucket stream listener + auto-cancelling subscription wrapper.
- `comments_list/comments_list_helpers.dart` — `commentEngagementScore` + `computeReplyCounts`.
- `comment_composer/mention_search.dart` — tier-1 local + tier-2 REST mention search returning plain records so the bloc owns the user-facing `MentionSuggestion` type.

### #4478 cache-key fix preserved

`rootAddressableId` is injected into all three blocs at construction. Every `postComment` / `deleteComment` / `loadComments` call site verifies the addressable-id thread-through via `verify()` (three explicit "(#4478)" tests in the new bloc test files). Three new outbox-emission tests guard the optimistic-placeholder reconciliation including the relay-echo-arrives-first race that `_onNewCommentReceived` resolves by matching placeholder by author+content.

## Type of Change

- [ ] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🛠️ Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] ❌ Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change)
- [x] 🧹 Code refactor
- [ ] ✅ Build configuration change
- [ ] 📝 Documentation
- [ ] 🗑️ Chore

## Verification

- `flutter test test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — **133/133 pass**, including 17 reactions tests, 20 composer tests, 24 list-bloc tests, and 72 widget tests covering the new `MultiBlocProvider` tree.
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` — **0 issues**.
- `dart format --set-exit-if-changed lib/blocs/comments/ lib/screens/comments/ test/blocs/comments/ test/screens/comments/` — clean.
- `wc -l` each successor bloc:
  - `comments_list_bloc.dart` — 497 lines
  - `comment_composer_bloc.dart` — 498 lines
  - `comment_reactions_bloc.dart` — 388 lines

## Manual test plan

- [ ] Open comments sheet on a NIP-71 addressable video → list loads.
- [ ] Type and send a comment → placeholder appears immediately; settles to real id on relay echo.
- [ ] Edit own comment → original removed and replacement appears in-place.
- [ ] Delete own comment → row disappears.
- [ ] Block another user → all their comments disappear from the open sheet.
- [ ] Upvote / downvote / switch / remove vote → net score updates optimistically, reverts on relay failure.
- [ ] Report a comment → no list mutation, no error toast.
- [ ] Cycle sort modes (New → Top → Old → New) → engagement sort reads upvote counts from reactions bloc through `comments_list.dart`'s nested `BlocSelector`.
- [ ] Edit a video that has ≥1 comment → re-open from profile → comment count does not drop to 0 (preserves #4478 cache fix).

## Acceptance criteria (from #4516)

- [x] Each successor bloc is under 500 lines. (497 / 498 / 388)
- [x] Existing comment widget tests pass after the split (provider-tree updated to `MultiBlocProvider`).
- [x] Cache-key fix from #4478 (addressable-edit dedup) is preserved.

title: refactor(notifications): classify NotificationFeedBloc invariants as Reportable (#4603)
body:
## Description

Follow-up to PR #4599 (comment-only matrix classification). That sweep
classified each of the 6 `addError(` sites in `NotificationFeedBloc` as
matrix-NO for the **Exception types they actually see**
(`FunnelcakeException`, `Exception('User not authenticated')`, relay/DAO
IO). The broad `catch (e, s)` still silently swallows **`Error`
subclasses** (`StateError`, `TypeError`, `RangeError`), which per
[`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#decision-matrix)
are matrix-YES.

This PR narrows each catch into two arms:

- `on Exception catch (e, s)` — matrix-NO domain failures, behavior
  unchanged (PR #4599 classification comment preserved verbatim).
- `catch (e, s)` — matrix-YES invariant violations, wrapped with
  `Reportable(e, context: NotificationFeedBlocReportableSites.xxx)` so
  `DivineBlocObserver` forwards them to Crashlytics. Recovery emit
  mirrors the matrix-NO arm so UX is preserved.

6 Reportable wraps > 2-site threshold → new
`mobile/lib/notifications/bloc/reportable_sites.dart` with stable
constants (per the lift-into-constants rule).

### Classification table

| # | Site (line) | Method | Repo call | matrix-NO arm sees | matrix-YES constant |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `_onStarted` | `refresh()` | `FunnelcakeException` (retried 5xx/timeout) | `onStarted` | |
| 2 | `_onLoadMore` | `getNotifications()` | `FunnelcakeException` (single-attempt) | `onLoadMore` | |
| 3 | `_onRefreshed` | `refresh()` | `FunnelcakeException` | `onRefreshed` | |
| 4 | `_onItemTapped` | `markAsRead()` | `FunnelcakeException`, Drift `SqliteException` | `onItemTapped` | |
| 5 | `_onMarkAllRead` | `markAllAsRead()` | `FunnelcakeException`, Drift `SqliteException` | `onMarkAllRead` | |
| 6 | `_onFollowBack` | `FollowRepository.follow()` | `Exception('User not authenticated')`, relay IO | `onFollowBack` | |

**Outcome: 6 matrix-YES sites added; 0 behavior changes; existing 8
`isA<Exception>()` blocTest assertions stay green** because
`Exception('boom')` still lands in the `on Exception catch` arm.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4603

## Out of Scope

- Narrowing the unreachable `Error.throwWithStackTrace(StateError('retry
  exhausted'))` defensive fallback in
  `NotificationRepository._fetchWithRetry`. If it ever fires it now
  surfaces as `Reportable<StateError>` from `_onStarted` /
  `_onRefreshed`, which is a free safety win. Repository-layer
  narrowing belongs in a separate follow-up.
- `_onSnapshotChanged` — pure projection, no try/catch, not one of the
  6 sites PR #4599 classified. Out of scope per the issue body.
- Other epic-#4336 sibling sweeps (DM, welcome/publish, video editor,
  profile editor, silent-failure remediation) — independent child
  issues.

## Verification

From `mobile/`:

- `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed` on all 3 changed
  files → `Formatted 3 files (0 changed)`.
- `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` → `No issues found! (ran in 33.4s)`.
- `flutter test test/notifications/bloc/notification_feed_bloc_test.dart` →
  24 tests passed (18 existing + 6 new Reportable-arm coverage).
- `flutter test test/notifications/` → 160 tests passed.

## Test plan

- [x] All 8 existing matrix-NO `errors: () => [isA<Exception>()]`
  blocTest assertions pass unchanged.
- [x] 6 new blocTests verify each site wraps `StateError`-throws as
  `Reportable<Object>.unwrap() is StateError`, with recovery emits
  identical to the matrix-NO branch.
- [x] Full `test/notifications/` suite (160 tests) green.
- [x] `flutter analyze` clean across `lib test integration_test`.
- [ ] CI green (Analyze + Tests + Format + Generated Files + build/build).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🧹 Code refactor

title: techdebt(notifications): classify unexpected NotificationFeedBloc invariants as Reportable
body:
## Problem
NotificationFeedBloc now documents which repository and domain failures are expected and not Reportable, but it still uses broad catch handlers at six call sites.

That is correct for preserving current recovery behavior, but it leaves adjacent error-handling debt: unexpected invariant failures such as StateError and TypeError are still only logged through addError(e, s) instead of being surfaced as Reportable(...) per .claude/rules/error_handling.md.

## Scope
Update mobile/lib/notifications/bloc/notification_feed_bloc.dart to separate expected-domain failures from unexpected invariant failures while preserving current UX behavior:

- Keep existing recovery emits and optimistic-rollback behavior unchanged.
- Handle expected repository and domain failures in typed on Exception catch blocks.
- Add a trailing generic catch path for unexpected failures and wrap those with Reportable(...) at the addError call site.
- Do not narrow catches without preserving the current fallback and loading-reset behavior.
- Add or update bloc tests to cover the reportable path and confirm existing recovery behavior still holds.

## Notes
This is follow-up debt adjacent to PR #4599, not a blocker for that comment-only change.

title: Search: support server-backed video sorting with stable pagination
body:
## Problem
Video search currently relies on local ordering and does not expose server-backed sort modes. That creates three concrete product issues:

- users cannot explicitly change how video search results are ranked
- progressive search / pagination can reorder or append stale results when the sort changes mid-request
- fullscreen playback can jump away from the active video when refreshed search results prepend or reshuffle items

## Goal
Ship server-backed video sorting for the Videos search filter and make the app preserve server ranking consistently across repository, bloc, and fullscreen-feed updates.

## Scope
- switch video search API calls to the server-backed search endpoint with `type=video`, `sort`, and cursor pagination support
- expose the supported sort modes in app state and the Videos search UI
- preserve API result order when combining local and remote search results
- prevent stale search-stream and load-more responses from one sort from mutating the state for another sort
- preserve the current fullscreen video by ID when result ordering changes
- cover the behavior with repository, bloc, widget, and fullscreen-feed tests

## Acceptance Criteria
- when the active search filter is Videos, the UI shows a sort control next to the filter pill
- selecting a sort reruns the current query with the new server-backed sort
- pagination uses the same selected sort and does not append results from an older in-flight sort
- repository-level progressive search keeps API-ranked results ahead of local fallback results without re-sorting them by legacy loops/time logic
- fullscreen feed stays pinned to the same video ID across reordered result updates when that video is still present
- localization copy for the new sort options is present and test-covered

## Non-goals
- adding new search types beyond videos
- changing profile search behavior
- redesigning the broader search screen layout beyond the video sort affordance

## Verification
- focused API client, repository, bloc, widget, fullscreen-feed, and localization tests pass
- `flutter analyze` passes for the touched areas
- manual device verification confirms the dual-pill layout fits on narrow screens

title: feat: document CAWG "do not train" assertion as Divine policy (and remove the unused opt-in path)
body:
### What would you like?

Document our existing CAWG `training-mining` assertion — embedded in the C2PA metadata of every published video — as **Divine policy**, not as a toggleable default. And remove the unused opt-in code path so it's truly the only option.

Current state on `main`:
- `C2paSigningService` embeds a `cawg.training-mining` assertion marking `ai_training`, `ai_inference`, `ai_generative_training`, and `data_mining` as `notAllowed`.
- `AiTrainingPreferenceService.isOptOutEnabled` defaults to `true` and is read by the publish / edit / clip providers.
- A `setOptOutEnabled(false)` API exists in the service but has no caller and no UI surface.

What's missing:
1. **User-facing docs** that say plainly: every video uploaded through Divine carries a cryptographically signed assertion opting the content out of AI training and data mining. This is policy, not a setting.
2. **Code hygiene** — remove `AiTrainingPreferenceService.setOptOutEnabled(false)` and the `aiTrainingOptOut: false` branches so the assertion is unconditional. Either keep the service as a thin always-on sentinel or inline the constant at the call sites.
3. **Coverage audit** — confirm every upload path embeds the assertion (camera record → publish, video editor → publish, clip → publish, plus any web / repost paths).

### How would this be useful for you?

Two reasons:

1. **Creator clarity.** Creators picking Divine should know that uploading here automatically attaches a CAWG-compliant "do not train" signal to their content. That's a meaningful trust signal vs. platforms that either don't mark content or bury the toggle.
2. **Transparent framing.** Like `robots.txt` or "do not track," the assertion will be ignored by bad actors. The value isn't technical prevention — it's a cryptographically signed line in the sand. The docs should say that plainly rather than overpromise.

Keeping it as "the only option" matters: if Divine ever exposes an opt-in toggle, the signal weakens for every other Divine creator (bad actors can then argue ambiguity). Unconditional protects everyone uploading here.

### When would you use this?

- New creators evaluating Divine want to know what protections their content carries.
- Press / partner / legal conversations where we need to point to a written policy.
- Inevitable "why doesn't Divine let me opt in to training?" support questions — we want one clear answer to link.

### Anything else?

Spec we follow: [CAWG Training and Data Mining v1.1](https://cawg.io/training-and-data-mining/1.1/)

Existing implementation pointers:
- `mobile/lib/services/c2pa_signing_service.dart` — manifest builder
- `mobile/lib/services/ai_training_preference_service.dart` — to be simplified or removed
- `mobile/lib/providers/video_publish_provider.dart`, `video_editor_provider.dart`, `clip_manager_provider.dart` — call sites
- `mobile/test/services/c2pa_training_mining_assertion_test.dart` — existing tests; the "excludes assertion when opt-out disabled" case will need to be inverted to "always includes assertion"

Out of scope for this issue:
- Server-side enforcement or re-signing of older content
- Surfacing the assertion in an in-app metadata viewer (possible follow-up)
- Coordinating with relays / other Nostr clients on honoring the assertion

title: feat(recorder/library): clip trash bin with 30-day retention
body:
Closes #4547

## Summary

Replaces the recorder's destructive "delete last clip" gesture with a
two-layer safety net:

1. **Snackbar Undo (5 s)** — taps to the bottom-left button now schedule a
   soft-delete and show a "Clip moved to trash • Undo" snackbar. Undo
   restores the clip to its original tray position.
2. **30-day trash bin** — clips that aren't undone land in a new
   *Recently deleted* screen (accessible from the clips library), where
   they sit for 30 days before auto-purge. Each row offers Restore /
   Delete now, plus a single "Empty trash" action.

Library-tab deletes are routed through the same `softDelete` path so
both surfaces share one delete behavior. Icon swapped from
`arrowCounterClockwise` → `trash` so the affordance reads as
*destructive-but-recoverable* instead of *undo my last tap*.

Motivation: in-app feedback from `723glimmers` — accidentally tapped
"undo" while assembling a brownie-batter compilation and lost a step.
The undo button's icon promised reversibility but the action was a
single-tap, no-confirm, on-disk hard delete with no recovery.

## Architecture

- **Schema:** `clips.deleted_at` (nullable timestamp) + idx_clip_deleted_at.
  All existing read paths now filter `deleted_at IS NULL`.
- **`ClipLibraryService`** split into `softDelete` / `restore` /
  `hardDelete` / `getTrashedClips` / `purgeExpiredTrash`. `softDelete`
  optionally clears `draft_id` so a recorder-trashed clip lands in the
  library on restore rather than a stale session.
- **`ClipManagerNotifier`** tracks the pending deletion in state, commits
  it on `addClip` / `reorderClip` / `clearAll` / dispose so a fresh
  recording never leaks a half-undone state.
- **`ClipsLibraryBloc`** gains four events: `TrashLoadRequested`,
  `RestoreClips`, `HardDeleteClip`, `EmptyTrash`, plus `trashedClips`
  and `lastDeletedClipIds` on state.
- **`purgeExpiredTrash(retention: 30d)`** runs on app startup from
  `app_lifecycle_handler.dart` (best-effort, idempotent).

## Test plan

- [x] `flutter test test/services/clip_library_service_test.dart` — softDelete / restore / hardDelete / purgeExpiredTrash coverage
- [x] `flutter test test/blocs/clips_library` — 64 tests, including state-prop shape after new fields
- [x] `flutter test test/providers/clip_manager_provider_test.dart` — `scheduleDeleteLastClip` smoke
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/video_recorder` — both recording modes
- [x] `flutter test test/widgets/library test/screens/library_screen_test.dart` — library entry-point unchanged for existing flows
- [x] `flutter test test/l10n/arb_consistency_test.dart` — new keys allowlisted
- [x] `packages/db_client` migration test — schema add safe
- [ ] Manual: capture-mode tap → snackbar → Undo → restored
- [ ] Manual: capture-mode tap → snackbar dismiss → clip in *Recently deleted* → Restore → library
- [ ] Manual: classic-mode same flow

- treats Funnelcake's real mark-read success shape (`marked_count` / `marked_all`) as success even when no synthetic `success` field is present

Tracking child of epic #4336. PR C2 in the epic plan — addresses two silent-failure outliers surfaced during the round-9 BLoC audit.

Two BLoCs combine a high catch-block count with **zero** `addError(` calls, so async failures are completely invisible:

| BLoC | catch blocks | addError sites |
|------|-------------:|---------------:|
| `mobile/lib/blocs/comments/comments_bloc.dart` | 16 | 0 |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/share_sheet/share_sheet_bloc.dart` | 10 | 0 |

`comments_bloc.dart` is the canary: every catch silently resets a loading flag, so a failure surfaces to the user as a hung-spinner-that-stops-spinning with no recovery path. `share_sheet_bloc.dart` is the same shape on share actions.

This violates both [`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md) ("avoid adding new silent-failure patterns") and the epic's [Agent Execution Notes](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/issues/4336#:~:text=avoid%20adding%20new%20silent-failure%20patterns).

1. **Audit every catch block** in both BLoCs. For each, choose one of:

2. **For `comments_bloc` specifically**: every catch that resets `isLoadingMore: false` (or similar loading sentinel) must also emit a `CommentsError` status-enum value so the UI can render a real failure affordance, not a stop-spinning-but-blank state.

body:
## Description

Add `if (!isClosed)` guards around `addError` calls in Bloc methods invoked from a fire-and-forget context. Without the guard, the Reportable-matrix migration (#4336) is shipping new `addError` calls into closed-bloc races that surface as misleading nonfatal Crashlytics noise — exactly the noise the matrix is meant to suppress.

Closes #4605. Same bug class as #4393 (which targets the `add()` variant of the same race).

## Sites guarded

| File | Method | Fire-and-forget context | Sibling `add()` already guarded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mobile/lib/blocs/welcome/welcome_bloc.dart` | `_hydrateAccount` | `_hydrateProfiles(knownAccounts);` (no await/unawaited) from `_onWelcomeStarted` line 105 | n/a — no `add()` call here, only `addError` (new from #4592) |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/clips_library/clips_library_bloc.dart` | `_recoverAndReload` | `unawaited(_recoverAndReload(clips));` from `_onLoadRequested` line 142 | yes — sibling `add()` at line 374 is `!isClosed`-gated; this PR adds symmetric guard for `addError` at line 388 |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc.dart` | `_publishLike` | `unawaited(_publishLike(...))` at line 254 | yes — sibling `add()` at line 305 is `!isClosed`-gated; this PR adds symmetric guard for `addError` at line 296 |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/video_interactions/video_interactions_bloc.dart` | `_publishRepost` | `unawaited(_publishRepost(...))` at line 376 | yes — sibling `add()` at line 432 is `!isClosed`-gated; this PR adds symmetric guard for `addError` at line 420 |

The welcome + clips_library sites are the ones the issue body called out explicitly; the two `video_interactions` sites surfaced from the audit grep required by the issue's acceptance criteria.

## Why `Reportable(...)` only at some sites

The wrap-vs-raw choice was set by the earlier matrix-classification sweeps (#4592, #4604) and is independent of this lifecycle fix. Welcome and clips_library are matrix-NO (Drift/file IO) → raw `addError`. The two video_interactions sites are matrix-YES (publish-path invariants) → `Reportable(...)` wrap. This PR preserves each existing classification and only adds the surrounding `isClosed` guard.

## Audit pass

Per issue acceptance criterion 3 — `grep -rn "unawaited(" mobile/lib/blocs/` plus a manual check of each match's callee for `addError` reachability:

- `fullscreen_feed_bloc.dart` (2 `unawaited(_processCacheQueue())` calls) — no `addError` in file
- `video_volume_cubit.dart` (3 `unawaited(_persist())` calls) — no `addError` in file
- `audio_timing_cubit.dart` (`unawaited(_onPlaybackCompleted())`) — no `addError` in file
- `video_feed_bloc.dart` (2 `unawaited(...)` calls) — no `addError` in file
- `profile_liked_videos_bloc.dart`, `profile_reposted_videos_bloc.dart` — `unawaited(...catchError(Log.warning))`, catches locally; never reaches `addError`
- `background_publish_bloc.dart` (3 `unawaited(...)` calls) — repository service calls, no `addError` reachable; the one `addError` in the file (`_onBackgroundPublishStarted` line 69) is inside the event handler, not fire-and-forget
- `dm/conversation/conversation_bloc.dart` — `unawaited(_dmRepository.markConversationAsRead(...))`, repository call

No additional `unawaited(...)` sites remain.

## Adjacent patterns explicitly out of scope

Self-review surfaced two adjacent fire-and-forget-ish patterns that are **not** in this PR's scope because they have a different lifecycle contract:

- **Stream-subscription `onError: addError` tear-offs** (`dm/unread_count/dm_unread_count_cubit.dart:25`, `notifications/badge/notification_badge_cubit.dart:28`) — these subscriptions are explicitly cancelled in `close()`, so post-close emissions are not expected. If a stream still emits an error after cancellation it is a stream-implementation bug, not the close-race this issue targets.
- **`on<E>` event handlers that `await` then `addError` in catch** (e.g. `welcome_bloc.dart:225`) — these are tracked by the bloc machinery, not fire-and-forget. The same close race technically exists if `close()` lands during an `await`, but the issue body intentionally scopes itself to fire-and-forget. A broader sweep would be a separate issue.

Filing a follow-up issue would be appropriate if reviewers want the broader sweep tracked formally.

## Tests

Four new regression tests (one per site) follow a common shape:

1. Stub the in-flight async dependency with a `Completer.future`
2. Dispatch the triggering event
3. `await Future<void>.delayed(Duration.zero)` to let the handler reach the unawaited call
4. `await bloc.close()` while the future is still pending
5. `completer.completeError(...)` — catch arm runs post-close
6. Assert `_CapturingObserver.errors` is empty

The capturing observer is a small per-test-file class implementing `BlocObserver.onError`.

**Test meaningfulness verified empirically**: removing the guard from `welcome_bloc._hydrateAccount` causes the regression test to fail with `Expected: empty, Actual: [Exception: DB error]` (the observer captures the post-close `addError`). The Reportable-matrix migration (epic #4336) is correctly adding `addError(...)` to catch arms that previously only `Log.error`'d. A subset of those catches sit inside Bloc methods invoked from a fire-and-forget context (`unawaited(...)`, or an unawaited call returning `Future<void>` from a non-async handler). When the user navigates away before the background work resolves, the bloc closes — and the subsequent `addError` fires on a closed `BlocBase`, producing exactly the kind of nonfatal Crashlytics noise the migration is trying to keep low-signal.

Same bug class as #4393 (which targets `add` after close) and #3734 (closed). This issue is the addError variant.

## Known sites

| File:Line | Fire-and-forget context | catch arm |
|---|---|---|
| `mobile/lib/blocs/welcome/welcome_bloc.dart` `_hydrateAccount` | `_hydrateProfiles(knownAccounts);` (line 105 of post-#4600, no `await`/`unawaited`) | `addError(e, stackTrace)` newly added in PR #4600 — flagged by @mbradley in https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/pull/4600#pullrequestreview-4338186724 |
| `mobile/lib/blocs/clips_library/clips_library_bloc.dart:387` `_recoverAndReload` | `unawaited(_recoverAndReload(clips));` at line 142 | `addError(e, stackTrace)` (pre-existing; classified matrix-NO in PR #4604). The sibling `add(ClipsLibraryLoadRequested(...))` IS already `!isClosed`-guarded; the `addError` is not. |

A broader audit may surface additional sites — see the `grep` in **Investigation** below.

## Why this matters now

Pre-migration these catches only logged locally — a post-close call was effectively a no-op. Post-migration `addError` flows through `DivineBlocObserver` → unified log, and (when wrapped in `Reportable`) on to Crashlytics. Closed-bloc invocations can either throw `StateError('Cannot add new events after calling close')` or surface as misleading reports. Either outcome contradicts the matrix's "report invariant violations, suppress expected churn" intent.

## Suggested fix

Add an `if (!isClosed)` guard immediately before each `addError` in a fire-and-forget method:

```dart
} catch (e, stackTrace) {
  Log.error('...', name: 'XxxBloc', error: e, stackTrace: stackTrace);
  if (!isClosed) {
    addError(e, stackTrace);
  }
}
```

The `Log.error` line stays unguarded — local logging is safe regardless of close state and remains useful for triage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both known sites (welcome `_hydrateAccount`, clips_library `_recoverAndReload`) carry an `if (!isClosed)` guard before `addError`.
- [ ] A `blocTest` per site that:
  - kicks off the fire-and-forget path,
  - `await bloc.close()` before the background future completes,
  - asserts `errors: () => const <Object>[]` (no addError-on-closed) and that no unhandled exception was recorded.
- [ ] Audit pass: grep `mobile/lib/blocs/` for `unawaited(` and for unawaited `Future<...>`-returning method calls from non-async handlers; classify each. Any additional addError-in-fire-and-forget sites that surface during the audit get the same guard + test, or get an inline comment explaining why the race is not reachable in their case.

## Investigation entry-points

```sh
# Fire-and-forget callers
grep -rn "unawaited(" mobile/lib/blocs/

# Methods called without await/unawaited from sync handlers (harder to catch
# by grep — look at handler bodies for bare `_methodName();` calls returning
# Future<void>).
```

Related: #4393, #4396 (widget-level `mounted` guards — analogous concept, different layer), #3734 (closed).

## Out of scope

- Widget-level `mounted` checks (covered by #4396).
- Changing the matrix classification of the affected catches — that landed in the sweep PRs (#4600, #4604).
- A general policy change about how every fire-and-forget bloc method should be structured. This issue is the targeted fix; if a broader policy is wanted it can fork off into a separate rule.

## Parent

Epic #4336.

title: feat(keycast): mid-session token refresh on 401 and app resume
body:
## Summary

Fixes #4588

Keycast OAuth tokens expire after ~3 hours. Users who leave the app backgrounded (common with iOS background modes for push notifications) return to a stale token and all RPC-backed operations (reporting, signing, encryption) fail silently — this was the root cause behind reporting surfaces failing (#4586).

Two recovery paths:

- **On app resume (Option A):** `AuthService.onAppResumed()` now checks if the stored OAuth session has expired and proactively refreshes it before any RPC call is attempted.
- **On 401 response (Option B):** `KeycastRpc._call()` detects 401 responses and invokes a `TokenRefreshCallback` to obtain a fresh access token, then retries the request once. This catches tokens that expire mid-session without an intervening app backgrounding.

Both paths share the same refresh mechanism via `OAuthClient.refreshSession()`.

### Changes

**`keycast_flutter` package:**
- Added `TokenRefreshCallback` typedef
- `KeycastRpc` constructor accepts optional `onTokenRefresh` callback
- `KeycastRpc.fromSession()` factory forwards `onTokenRefresh`
- `_call()` detects 401, invokes callback, updates token, retries once
- Extracted `_sendRequest()` to avoid duplication between initial call and retry

**`auth_service.dart`:**
- Added `_refreshAccessToken()` — the callback wired into every `KeycastRpc` instance
- Added `_refreshOAuthTokenOnResume()` — proactive refresh on app resume when session is expired
- Wired `onTokenRefresh: _refreshAccessToken` at all three `KeycastRpc.fromSession()` construction sites (init, background upgrade, signInWithDivineOAuth)

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new tests for 401 retry behavior in `rpc_client_test.dart`
- [x] All 178 `keycast_flutter` package tests pass
- [x] Analyzer clean on both changed files
- [ ] Manual: sign in with Divine OAuth, wait for token expiry (~3 hours or force-expire in staging), trigger a report/sign operation → should succeed transparently
- [ ] Manual: background app past token expiry, resume → RPC operations should work without re-login

title: Keycast OAuth token expiry during background silently breaks all write operations
body:
## Summary

When the app is backgrounded long enough for the Keycast OAuth token to expire (~3 hours), all write operations fail silently on resume. `KeycastRpc._call()` throws `RpcException` on HTTP 401 but no caller catches it to attempt a token refresh and retry. The user gets no re-auth prompt -- operations just fail.

This affects every RPC-only (`divineOAuth`, no local nsec) user. With `UIBackgroundModes: fetch, remote-notification` enabled (added with push notification support in #2848), iOS keeps the app process alive during extended background periods, making this a common scenario rather than an edge case.

## Affected operations

Everything that signs a Nostr event via Keycast RPC:
- Content/user reports (NIP-56 kind 1984)
- Video uploads (NIP-98 auth for Blossom)
- Push notification registration (kind 3079)
- Event publishing (likes, reposts, comments, DMs)
- Any other `sign_event` call

## Root cause

`KeycastRpc` bakes the access token in at construction time and uses it for the lifetime of the instance. When the token expires server-side, every `_call()` throws:

```
RpcException [sign_event]: HTTP 401: {"error":"Invalid or expired token. Please log in again."}
```

The refresh infrastructure exists but isn't wired to mid-session failures:
- `OAuthClient.refreshSession()` and `getSessionOrRefresh()` can obtain fresh tokens
- `AuthService.tryRefreshExpiredSession()` can refresh and rebuild identity
- `AuthService._hasExpiredOAuthSession` tracks the expiry state
- The Settings screen shows a "Session Expired" tile when the flag is set

But:
- `_hasExpiredOAuthSession` is only set during `initialize()` and `signInForAccount()` -- never on a mid-session 401
- `AuthService.onAppResumed()` reconnects bunker signers and nostrconnect relays but does not check/refresh the OAuth token
- No caller of `KeycastRpc._call()` catches `RpcException` to attempt refresh-and-retry

## Why this wasn't visible before

Before push notification support (#2848, April 2026), the app did not declare `UIBackgroundModes`. iOS would kill the process more aggressively during extended background, leading to cold launches that run `AuthService.initialize()` -> `refreshSession()` -> fresh token. Push notifications added `UIBackgroundModes: fetch, remote-notification`, which tells iOS to keep the process alive for push delivery -- making warm resumes (with stale tokens) the common path instead of cold launches (with token refresh).

## Log evidence

From `openvine_full_logs_2026-05-20T17-33-22`:

```
[10:24:46] App launch -- signing succeeds (kind 27235, kind 3079)
[10:25:55] App enters background
[12:59:49] Delayed background suspension (process still alive after ~2.5 hours)
[13:26:54] App resumes -- first sign_event -> HTTP 401
[13:26:54+] Every subsequent sign_event fails with 401 for the rest of the session
```

The app resumed ~20 times after the first 401 failure. `onAppResumed()` ran each time. No token refresh was ever attempted.

## Suggested fix directions

**Option A: Refresh on resume** -- `AuthService.onAppResumed()` checks token expiry via `KeycastSession.isExpired` and calls `refreshSession()` before any signing attempt. Simplest, handles the common "came back from background" case.

**Option B: Retry on 401** -- Wrap `KeycastRpc._call()` (or the signing path in `NostrIdentity`) with catch-401 -> `refreshSession()` -> reconstruct `KeycastRpc` -> retry. Handles mid-foreground expiry too, but more invasive.

**Option C: Proactive refresh** -- Schedule a timer based on `KeycastSession.expiresAt` to refresh before expiry. Most robust but adds complexity.

These aren't mutually exclusive -- A is cheap and covers the main scenario, B/C are additive.

## Related

- #4586 -- Reporting surfaces failing silently (symptom of this issue for reports)
- PR #4587 -- Inline error display for reports (makes signing failures visible, doesn't fix the token expiry)
- PR #4444 -- Fix local nsec export for Keycast-backed accounts (acknowledges RPC-only account type)
- PR #4162 -- Session readiness gating (stabilized provider lifecycle, `KeycastRpc` instances live longer)
- #2848 -- Push notification support (added `UIBackgroundModes` that changed background process lifetime)

  Please look at the following checklist to ensure that your PR can be accepted quickly:

## Description
The retryCount stored in Hive was never incremented between retry cycles. _performUploadWithRetry read retryCount from the persisted PendingUpload, then wrote it back unchanged (retryCount: currentRetry instead of retryCount: currentRetry + 1). Every iteration therefore read 0, logged "Upload attempt 1/6", and wrote 0 back — the counter was frozen and the status never transitioned from uploading to retrying.

The user in #4142 saw "Upload attempt 1/6" repeated across all six attempts with no indication that retries were progressing. - retryCount increments after each failed attempt (1 → 2 over a fail-then-succeed cycle)
- status transitions from uploading on attempt 1 to retrying on attempt 2

## Description
When the user checks 'I am 18 or older' in Safety Settings, set all three adult categories (nudity, sexual, porn) to ContentFilterPreference.show so that MediaAuthInterceptor auto-creates auth headers for age-restricted videos.

Previously, setAdultContentVerified(true) was called but per-category prefs stayed at their default hide. adultPlaybackPreference then resolved to hide, causing MediaAuthInterceptor to return null even for verified users — so age-restricted videos always got a 401 and never played.

The unlock is symmetric with the existing lockAdultCategories() call that runs when the user un-checks the box.

### Classification table

Bundled asset ships inside the IPA/APK so runtime `PlatformException` is essentially impossible. | Invariant | **YES (new)** → inline `context: '_onLoad'` |

| `_onProfileNip05Saved` (new outer wrap) | handler body | same | Invariant | **YES (new)** -> `onProfileNip05Saved` |

body:
## Description

Classification sweep over `welcome_bloc`, `divine_auth_cubit`, and the
`VideoEventPublisher._publishEventToNostr()` failure contract per the
[Reportable decision matrix](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#decision-matrix).

**Outcome: 0 new YES sites + 12 NO classifications + 1 documented
sentinel + 8 silent catches upgraded to `addError(e, stackTrace)`.**

No `reportable_sites.dart` is created (threshold is 2+ YES sites).
Matches the discipline of PR #4597 (DM area, merged) and PR #4599
(notifications, in flight).

### Classification table

| File:Line | Method | Catch sees | Matrix row | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `welcome_bloc.dart:135` | `_hydrateAccount` generic | `UserProfilesDao.getProfile` Drift IO | Network/IO | **NO** — was silent, now adds `addError(e, stackTrace)` |
| `welcome_bloc.dart:205` | `_onLogBackIn` on `SessionExpiredException` | session-refresh failure | Auth/session | NO |
| `welcome_bloc.dart:224` | `_onLogBackIn` generic | OAuth / Invite / network / signer restore | Mixed (dominant NO) | NO; narrowing deferred |
| `welcome_bloc.dart:267` | `_onCancelSwitch` on `SessionExpiredException` | same as `_onLogBackIn` | Auth/session | NO |
| `welcome_bloc.dart:273` | `_onCancelSwitch` generic | same as `_onLogBackIn` | Mixed (dominant NO) | NO; narrowing deferred |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:181` | `submit()` outer generic | `_handleSignIn`/`_handleSignUp` propagated failures | Mixed (dominant NO) | NO; narrowing deferred |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:340` | `_exchangeCodeAndLogin` on `InviteApiException` | invite activation rejected by API | API/domain | NO |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:363` | `_exchangeCodeAndLogin` on `OAuthException` | OAuth token exchange failure | Auth/session | NO |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:376` | `_exchangeCodeAndLogin` generic | storage / signing / identity / network | Mixed (dominant NO) | NO; narrowing deferred |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:416` | `sendPasswordResetEmail` generic | OAuth client network failures | Network/IO | NO |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:468` | `skipWithAnonymousAccount` on `InviteApiException` | invite activation rejected | API/domain | NO |
| `divine_auth_cubit.dart:490` | `skipWithAnonymousAccount` generic | key-gen / storage / identity | Mixed (dominant NO) | NO; narrowing deferred |
| `video_event_publisher.dart:235` | `_publishEventToNostr` | (sentinel return, see `///`) | Network/IO + API/domain | **documented sentinel** |

### Publisher contract decision (Option 2)

`_publishEventToNostr` is private with 4 internal callers (the
`publishDirectUpload` retry loop with exponential backoff, the two
audio-publish degrade-gracefully paths, and `republishWithSubtitles`).
All four treat `false` as a recoverable "this attempt didn't propagate"
signal and have explicit post-failure recovery.

| Option | Effort | Risk | Caller blast radius |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — throw `PublishFailedException` | ~40 LOC + new exception + 4 caller wrappers + ~5 tests | Behavior regression if retry loop loses a path | 4 internal sites need try/catch wrappers to preserve current `bool/null/false` semantics |
| **2 — document the `///` contract ✓** | ~30 LOC of dartdoc | Zero behavior change | No caller changes |

Per `error_handling.md` the inner failures are network/IO + API/domain
— matrix-NO — so even the `Reportable`-wrapped throw path would not
surface to Crashlytics. Option 2 also matches audit #3593's own
recommendation track-(b): "for intentionally-suppressing methods, add
`///` documentation explaining when null/false/[] is returned and why."

### Test changes

- `welcome_bloc_test.dart`: the existing "emits loaded with account
  when profile lookup throws" test is renamed and gets
  `errors: () => [isA<Exception>()]` to pin the new
  `_hydrateAccount` `addError` contract.
- `divine_auth_cubit_test.dart`: 8 existing failure-path blocTests
  gain `errors:` assertions (lines 413, 481, 672, 717, 1310, 1372,
  1452, 1492). Mirrors the call surface — no new tests.

No new files. No package changes. No regenerated codegen.

**Related Issue:** Closes #4592

## Out of Scope

- Removing `generalError: String?` from `DivineAuthState` (10
  emission sites). Tracked under epic #4336 → child **#3591**.
- Narrowing the dominant-NO generic auth-flow catches into typed
  invariant-YES paths. Analogous to PR #4597's deferral of
  `_onMessageSent`.
- Adding a reporter-port to `VideoEventPublisher` (service-layer
  observability, not a Bloc) — out of scope per the issue body which
  scopes only the failure-contract decision.
- Converting `_publishEventToNostr` to throw a typed exception
  (Option 1) — see decision matrix above.
- Sibling area sweeps under epic #4336: notifications (#4591),
  video-editor + clips + search (#4594), profile-editor (#4593),
  silent-failure remediation comments_bloc + share_sheet_bloc (#4595).

title: refactor(welcome,publish): classify Bloc errors via Reportable matrix and decide publish failure contract (#4336)
body:
Tracking child of epic #4336. One PR (PR D in the epic plan) classifying `addError(` sites in the welcome / auth / publish area against the [Reportable decision matrix](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md#decision-matrix), **and** deciding the failure contract for `VideoEventPublisher._publishEventToNostr()`.

## Scope

- `mobile/lib/blocs/welcome/welcome_bloc.dart` — 4 `addError` sites
- `mobile/lib/blocs/divine_auth/divine_auth_cubit.dart` — currently 0 `addError`, 7 catch blocks (silent-failure outlier)
- `mobile/lib/services/video_event_publisher.dart` — `_publishEventToNostr()` currently returns `false` for *silently not propagated to relays*. This is one of the most-cited examples in the audit (#3593) of an undocumented sentinel-return contract.

This area has **zero** migrated sites today; this PR lands the first example so the precedent exists for future contributors.

## Two contract decisions in this PR

1. **welcome / divine_auth**: pure classification per the matrix. Most sites will be auth/network/IO → NO (matrix non-reportable). The `divine_auth_cubit` 7 silent-catch sites need at minimum `addError(e, stackTrace)` so failures stop disappearing — Reportable classification can come on top.
2. **`VideoEventPublisher._publishEventToNostr()`**: pick **one** of:
   - Throw a typed `PublishFailedException` from the publisher (then update callers).
   - Document the `false` contract explicitly in the method's `///` doc per the audit's "intentional sentinel" guidance.

Both are valid per the matrix as long as the contract is explicit. Prefer (1) if the call-site count is small; prefer (2) if callers are scattered.

## Acceptance

- [ ] welcome + divine_auth: every `addError(` and every silent catch in scope classified; PR description includes a `(site, matrix row, decision)` table.
- [ ] YES sites wrap with `Reportable(e, context: ...)`. Multi-site files use a colocated `*ReportableSites` constants file.
- [ ] `divine_auth_cubit` silent catches get at minimum `addError(e, stackTrace)`; failures are no longer invisible.
- [ ] `_publishEventToNostr()`: decision documented; either a typed throw or a `///` contract block listing the `false` cause.
- [ ] Tests updated; `flutter analyze lib test integration_test` green.

## Risk

Medium — touches auth + publish paths. Profile a publish cold start before/after to confirm no observable latency change.

## References

- Epic: #4336
- Spec: [`.claude/rules/error_handling.md`](https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-mobile/blob/main/.claude/rules/error_handling.md)
- Source audit: #3593 (cited the publish-path sentinel as a Medium-to-High-risk example)

title: refactor(state): define and enforce Riverpod/BLoC migration boundaries
body:
Source audit context: fresh `origin/main` worktree `.worktrees/audit-codebase-2026-04-24` at commit `33f6e026a`.
This issue was generated from the April 2026 codebase audit and includes file/line evidence from that snapshot.

## Severity
High

## Problem
Docs say BLoC/Cubit is the default for UI state, but UI paths still mix Riverpod providers, BLoC providers, service notifiers, and bridge providers without a clear ownership boundary.

## Evidence
- docs/STATE_MANAGEMENT.md:12 says BLoC/Cubit is the default for UI state.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:12 says mixed Riverpod + BLoC + service notifiers increase cognitive load.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:39 prefers BLoC/Cubit for new UI state.
- docs/BLOC_UI_MIGRATION_PRD.md:110 warns against Riverpod bridges without TODO/issue linkage.
- mobile/lib/router/app_shell.dart:37 is a ConsumerStatefulWidget while :528 reads DmUnreadCountCubit via context.watch.
- mobile/lib/notifications/view/notifications_page.dart:17 is a ConsumerWidget that creates a BlocProvider.
- mobile/lib/screens/apps/apps_directory_screen.dart:16 is a ConsumerWidget that creates a BlocProvider.
- mobile/lib/screens/explore_screen.dart:50 remains a large Riverpod-driven UI screen while feed-related BLoCs exist elsewhere.

## Impact
New code can accidentally extend the hybrid model instead of shrinking it. Ownership of UI state, side effects, and rebuilds remains unclear.

## Recommended fix
Define an explicit boundary: Riverpod owns app-level DI and long-lived services; BLoC/Cubit owns feature UI state and UI side effects; temporary bridges need issue links and removal criteria.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Architecture docs include concrete allowed/disallowed patterns.
- [ ] Current bridge widgets/providers are identified and linked to migration issues.
- [ ] One representative mixed screen is converted to Page/View split as a template.
- [ ] Review/lint guidance prevents new long-lived Riverpod UI providers.
- [ ] Docs reference current issue numbers and no stale migration claims.
